correctness.rationale: Strict upper cones are exactly x+H_+. If y<x, y+m (m=min H_+) is in the upper cone of y but not of x, so inclusion fails. For d=y−x≥0, translated upper-cone inclusion iff d+H_+⊆H_+, equivalent to d∈H or d pseudo-Frobenius. Adding all PF numbers preserves additive closure: for d1,d2 in PF and s in H_+, d2+s lies in H_+, so d1+(d2+s) lies in H; therefore d1+d2 is either already in H or itself is PF. This handles PF+PF products and makes induction valid. Frobenius number is PF, thus each stage removes >=1 gap; exact gap-count telescoping gives genus=sum of types. Independently enumerated H=<4,7> gaps [1,2,3,5,6,9,10,13,17], PF=[17]; this is a check, not a proof.
